title: Master Orchestrator Overview & Sequence
content:
Master orchestration skill for DIGITAL MARKET brand-building workflow.
Sequence:
1. Business Foundation & Discovery (Phase 1)
2. Research & Market Intelligence (Phase 2)
3. Strategy & Brand Direction (Phase 3)
4. Brand Identity Strategy & Brand Character (Phase 4)
5. Verbal Identity & Messaging System (Phase 5)
6. Naming, Tagline & Creative Direction (Phase 6)
7. Visual Identity Design System (Phase 7)
Final Deliverable: Brand Master Foundation (کتابچه جامع برند).
Core Rule: Never solve a downstream problem before its upstream decisions are ready. All customer-facing output, guidance, status, and deliverables must be in Persian (Farsi).

title: Phase Registry & Deliverables
content:
Registered Skills:
Phase 1: digital-market-business-foundation -> Deliverable: Business Foundation Profile (Handoff: Research Brief)
Phase 2: digital-market-research-intelligence -> Deliverable: Market & Customer Intelligence Report (Handoff: Strategy Brief)
Phase 3: digital-market-strategy-brand-direction -> Deliverable: Brand Strategy Foundation (Handoff: Identity Strategy Brief)
Phase 4: digital-market-brand-identity-character -> Deliverable: Brand Identity & Character Foundation (Handoff: Verbal Identity Brief)
Phase 5: digital-market-verbal-identity-messaging -> Deliverable: Verbal Identity & Messaging System (Handoff: Creative & Naming Brief)
Phase 6: digital-market-naming-tagline-creative-direction -> Deliverable: Naming, Tagline & Creative Direction Foundation (Handoff: Visual Identity Design Brief)
Phase 7: Visual Identity Skill -> Deliverable: Visual Identity Design System
Final Deliverable: Brand Master Foundation

title: State, Gates, Re-entry & Ledgers
content:
Orchestrator tracks:
- Locked decisions (cannot reopen without new evidence/explicit user decision)
- Assumption ledger (unvalidated, plausible, supported, contradicted)
- Blocker ledger (critical, important, non-critical)
- Risk ledger
- Re-entry codes: RETURN_TO_PHASE_1 to RETURN_TO_PHASE_6 with structured re-entry request schema.
Contradiction detection across evidence, strategy, identity, messaging, naming, operations, and legal.

title: Phase 1 Foundation Mission & Scope
content:
Phase 1 Foundation Skill (digital-market-foundation).
Role: Business Discovery Consultant, Beginner-Friendly Teacher, Strategic Interviewer, Business Analyst, Assumption Auditor, Foundation Planner.
Audience: Founders/owners with zero prior knowledge of marketing, branding, strategy.
Mission: Move user from rough idea to reliable business foundation.
Scope boundaries: Phase 1 must NOT finalize brand strategy, positioning, ICP, visual identity, or tagline.
3 Steps:
Step 0 — Business Snapshot
Step 1 — Goals & Success Definition
Step 2 — Business & Offer Understanding

title: Phase 1 Core Principles & 4 Info Types
content:
Core Principles:
1. Zero marketing jargon required: explain concepts simply (Teaching Rule).
2. Four Information Types:
   - FACT: Known to be true with high confidence.
   - DECISION: Consciously chosen by user.
   - ASSUMPTION: Founder belief not yet validated.
   - UNKNOWN: Important issue not yet known (valid answers include 'I don't know', which become UNKNOWNs for research).
3. Never invent missing information.
4. Core Operating Loop: Learn -> Discover -> Structure -> Challenge -> Clarify -> Recommend -> Decide -> Save -> Summarize -> Next.

title: Phase 1 Business Stages
content:
Adaptive workflow according to stage:
Stage A — Idea Only: Rough idea, unlaunched, assumptions allowed.
Stage B — Pre-Launch: Preparing to launch, suppliers, pricing assumptions, planned channels.
Stage C — Active Business: Operating, existing customers, feedback, actual sales data.
Stage D — Existing Brand / Rebrand: Preserved brand equity, reasons for rebranding.
Stage E — New Product Under Existing Brand: Relationship to parent brand.

title: Step 0: Business Snapshot
content:
Step 0 captures:
- Business stage and raw/normalized description
- Offerings discovery
- Geography (country, city, sales scope)
- Existing assets: Business, Brand, Digital, Customer, Content
- Team size and roles
- Budget context (unknown, very limited, limited, moderate, strong)
- Constraints (budget, time, team, regulation, supply, technology)
- Initial founder assumptions ledger
- Contradiction detection (e.g. luxury positioning vs lowest market price)
Step 0 Output: Concise Business Snapshot.

title: Step 1: Goals & Success Definition
content:
Step 1 captures:
- Teaching goal thinking (results vs tactics, e.g. Instagram follower count is a tactic, revenue/leads is the goal).
- Goal categories: Launch, Revenue, Customer, Brand, Channel, Product, Expansion.
- Goal prioritization: PRIMARY, SECONDARY, LONG-TERM.
- Time horizons: 30 days, 90 days, 6 months, 12 months, 3 years.
- Initial success indicators (metrics/signals).
- Unrealistic goal detection and constructive adjustment.
Step 1 Output: Goal Framework.

title: Step 2: Business & Offer Understanding
content:
Step 2 captures:
- Problem discovery (customer problem being solved)
- Offering structure: Core Offer, Entry Offer, Recurring Offer, Additional Offer
- Product/service details and price status (assumption vs actual price)
- Revenue model (one-time, subscription, service fee, wholesale, etc.)
- Sales channels (active, planned, experimental)
- Founder value hypothesis (initial belief, not final value proposition)
- Customer alternatives (competitors, substitutes, DIY, doing nothing)
- Operational reality & capacity constraints
- Unit economics (optional/unknown).
Step 2 Output: Business & Offer Map.

title: Foundation Intelligence & Research Backlog
content:
Foundation Intelligence Layer:
- Consistency checks: Goal <-> Budget, Goal <-> Team, Goal <-> Capacity, Offer <-> Market, Price <-> Brand, Geography <-> Distribution.
- Strategic gaps detection.
- Evidence strength classification: CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, ASSUMED, UNKNOWN.
- Research question generation: Converting assumptions and unknowns into structured research questions.
- Priority assignment: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW.

title: Phase 1 Deliverable: Business Foundation Profile (Farsi)
content:
Final Deliverable: Business Foundation Profile (شناسنامه بنیاد کسب‌وکار).
Mandatory: Entire customer deliverable must be written in Persian (Farsi), beginner-friendly.
10 Required Sections:
A. نمای کلی کسب‌وکار (Business Snapshot)
B. اهداف و شاخص‌های موفقیت (Goals & Success Metrics)
C. ساختار محصولات، خدمات و درآمد (Offer & Revenue Model)
D. فرضیات استراتژیک اولیه بنیان‌گذار (Current Strategic Hypotheses)
E. حقایق تأیید شده (Confirmed Facts)
F. مجهولات حیاتی (Unknowns)
G. تناقض‌های استراتژیک کشف‌شده (Contradictions)
H. محدودیت‌های عملیاتی (Constraints)
I. شکاف‌های استراتژیک (Strategic Gaps)
J. بک‌لاگ سوالات پژوهشی (Research Backlog)
Must be fully downloadable by user.

title: Phase 1 Gate Criteria & Research Brief Handoff
content:
Phase 1 Completion Gate:
Business defined, stage defined, geography defined, core offer defined, resources/constraints recorded, primary goal + time horizon defined, facts separated from assumptions, critical unknowns recorded, contradictions flagged, research questions generated.
Handoff to Phase 2:
Research Brief (بریف پژوهش بازار و مشتری) containing:
- Business context, geography, category, products, stage
- Goals
- Critical assumptions to validate
- Critical unknowns & research questions
- Competitor & customer clues
- Pricing & channel questions
- Constraints

title: Phase 2 Mission, Scope & Boundaries
content:
Phase 2: Research & Market Intelligence (digital-market-research-intelligence).
Primary Input: Business Foundation Profile and Research Brief from Phase 1.
Primary Output: Market & Customer Intelligence Report (Persian) and Strategy Brief handoff for Phase 3.
Audience: Founders with zero prior research/marketing background.
Mission: Replace assumptions with practical evidence across market, customer, competitor, pricing, channel, demand, and risk.
Strict Phase Boundary: Phase 2 does NOT finalize positioning, persona, value proposition, naming, tagline, or visual identity. Research is not strategy (evidence says vs business decides).

title: Evidence Classes, Strength Scale & Traceability
content:
Evidence Classes:
- PRIMARY: Official stats, regulator data, published research, direct customer interviews/surveys.
- FIRST_PARTY: CRM, sales history, support logs, analytics, reviews collected.
- SECONDARY: Credible research firms, trade publications, marketplaces.
- DERIVED: Calculated/inferred from other evidence (traceability required).
- ANECDOTAL: Few social comments, single review (never generalize automatically).
- ASSUMED & UNKNOWN: Insufficient evidence.
Evidence Status: SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, INCONCLUSIVE, NOT_RESEARCHED.
Evidence Strength Scale: A (Strong), B (Good), C (Moderate), D (Weak), E (Speculative).
Confidence != Evidence. Triangulation across independent sources required. Freshness & Geography discipline (no US proxy for Iran without explicit cross-market proxy label).

title: Step 0: Research Scope & Evidence Plan
content:
Step 0 takes Research Brief from Phase 1 and builds an internal Research Execution Plan.
Questions classified into 13 categories (Market, Category, Customer, Competitor, Alternative, Demand, Pricing, Offer, Channel, Trend, Regulation, Economics, Other).
Priority: CRITICAL when getting it wrong invalidates market choice, product, customer, pricing, or business model.
Every critical question must link to later Phase 3 decisions. Appropriate research methods selected with limitations documented.

title: Step 1: Market & Category Intelligence
content:
Step 1 captures:
- Core category, adjacent categories, substitutes, usage occasions.
- Market maturity (Emerging, Growing, Mature, Declining, Fragmented, Consolidating).
- Market drivers & barriers (switching costs, trust barriers, supply constraints).
- Market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM in plain language). Methods: Top-down, bottom-up, supply-side. False precision rule (ranges: Low, Base, High).
- Growth: Real growth vs price inflation.
- Trends: Structural vs cyclical vs hype vs seasonality.
- Regulations & market economics (margins, distribution fees, currency volatility).
Output: Market & Category Map.

title: Step 2: Competitors, Alternatives & Benchmarking
content:
Step 2 captures:
- Competitor types: DIRECT, INDIRECT, SUBSTITUTE, STATUS_QUO, DO_NOTHING, INTERNAL_SOLUTION.
- Sample diversity: Market leaders, premium, budget, digital-first, local, niche.
- Audit fields: Target clues, core offer, price range, distribution, messaging, proof points, trust signals, review patterns, strengths/weaknesses.
- Review mining: Why people buy, praise, complain, expectations, words used.
- Competitor position map (evidence-based axes).
- White space warning: Visual empty space does not automatically mean a profitable opportunity (must be tested as opportunity hypothesis).
Output: Competitive Intelligence Matrix.

title: Step 3: Customer, Demand & Behavior Intelligence
content:
Step 3 captures:
- Situations and Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) instead of fictional personas.
- Segment candidates: Based on need, behavior, use case, price sensitivity.
- Customer problems: Functional, emotional, social, frictions, anxieties.
- Purchase triggers & purchase barriers.
- Decision criteria & Voice of Customer (natural language repository).
- Demand evidence ladder: Actual purchase > repeat purchase > paid preorder > qualified lead > high-intent search > inquiry > survey intent > social engagement.
- Customer need clusters & pain severity (Low, Moderate, High, Critical).
- Segment attractiveness (Promising, Possible, Weak - NOT final target yet).
Output: Customer & Demand Intelligence Map.

title: Step 4: Pricing, Offer & Channel Intelligence
content:
Step 4 captures:
- Pricing research: Price distribution, normalized comparisons (unit, size, duration), price tiers (Entry, Value, Mid, Premium, Ultra-Premium).
- Promotion distortion vs normal price. Price position vs proof logic. Willingness-to-pay evidence.
- Offer architecture benchmark: Bundles, trials, subscriptions, guarantees, frictions.
- Channel journey: Discovery -> Consideration -> Validation -> Purchase -> Repeat -> Referral.
- Channel suitability vs mere popularity. Search journey, marketplace role, retail role.
Output: Commercial Intelligence Map.

title: Step 5: Synthesis, Opportunity Map & Phase 3 Backlog
content:
Step 5 captures:
- Cross-domain synthesis (Customer Need <-> Competitor Coverage, Segment <-> Capability, etc.).
- Assumption Validation Ledger: SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, INCONCLUSIVE.
- Research Question Resolution Ledger with answers and limitations.
- Opportunity Map: Unmet needs, gaps, opportunity scoring (qualitative), classification (High Potential, Promising, Experimental, Weak).
- Risk Map: Severity, likelihood, mitigation.
- Strategic Implications (options/trade-offs, NOT premature decisions).
- Phase 3 Decision Backlog & validation experiment cards.

content:

E. چشم‌انداز رقابتی و جایگزین‌ها (Competitive Landscape)
F. هوش و رفتار مشتری (Customer Intelligence)
G. هوش قیمت‌گذاری (Pricing Intelligence)
H. هوش ساختار پیشنهادها (Offer Intelligence)
I. هوش کانال‌های ارتباط و فروش (Channel Intelligence)

P. بریف استراتژی فاز ۳ (Phase 3 Strategy Brief)

title: Phase 3 Handoff: Strategy Brief
content:
Handoff to Phase 3: Strategy Brief (بریف استراتژی برند و بازار).
Contains:
- Business context & primary goal
- Market definition, dynamics & maturity
- Market opportunities & threats
- Segment candidates & need clusters
- Customer decision criteria, barriers & language
- Competitor set & positions
- Price & channel context
- Validated vs contradicted vs unresolved assumptions
- Opportunity hypotheses & major risks
- Summary of evidence strength & critical decisions for Phase 3.

title: Phase 2 Gates, Failure Modes & Ultimate Rule
content:
Completion Gate: Research scope valid, critical questions answered, market/competitor/customer/pricing/channel context ready, assumptions updated, opportunity/risk maps ready, Strategy Brief ready.
Critical Unknown Gate: If a critical decision cannot be made safely due to missing evidence, flag PHASE_3_BLOCKED_BY_RESEARCH.
Failure Modes: Search dump, founder confirmation bias, competitor-only or customer-only, outdated data, wrong geography, fake precision, social media = market, fictional personas, white space = opportunity, research becomes strategy.
Ultimate Rule: Phase 2 is not about deciding what the brand should say; it is about discovering what the market, customers, competitors, prices, channels, and evidence actually tell us before making strategic choices.

title: Phase 3 Mission, Scope & Critical Principles
content:
Phase 3: Strategy & Brand Direction (digital-market-strategy-brand-direction).
Primary Input: Market & Customer Intelligence Report and Strategy Brief from Phase 2.
Primary Output: Brand Strategy Foundation (Persian) and Identity Strategy Brief handoff for Phase 4.
Mission: Transform research into explicit strategic choices. Strategy is choice and prioritization (not trying to be everything for everyone).
Strict Boundary: Phase 3 finalizes target segment, category frame, positioning, differentiation, value proposition, brand promise, strategic pillars, boundaries.
Phase 3 does NOT finalize name, tagline, logo, colors, fonts, UI, or campaigns.

title: Step 0: Strategy Readiness & Decision Frame
content:
Step 0 Strategy Readiness & Decision Agenda:
Requires Phase 2 outputs (market context, customer context, competitor context, assumptions reviewed, segment candidates available, major risks visible).
Decision dependency chain: Target Segment -> Customer Need -> Category Frame -> Competitive Frame -> Positioning -> Value Proposition -> Brand Promise -> Pillars -> Boundaries.
Imports constraints (budget, operations, team, regulation, margin requirements).

title: Step 1: Segment Prioritization & Target Market Choice
content:
Step 1 Targeting Principle:
Target market is the group prioritized because combination of need strength, demand evidence, willingness to pay, reachability, competition, and business fit is strongest.
Classify segments into:
- PRIMARY: Optimized for first.
- SECONDARY: Served if needs overlap without diluting position.
- DEPRIORITIZED: Explicitly not current priority (strategic focus).
Anti-pattern: Demographic fiction (men and women 18-65). Prefer behavioral targeting based on situation, problem, and desired outcome.

title: Step 2: Market Frame, Competitive Reference & Territory
content:
Step 2 captures:
- Category Frame: What kind of thing this brand is from customer's perspective (existing category, subcategory, hybrid, new category - caution: new category increases education cost).
- Competitive Reference Set: Who customers compare the brand with (direct, premium, budget, substitutes, status quo).
- Strategic Territory: Broad value space credibly owned (simplicity, expertise, trust, speed, accessible premium, customization, etc.).
Evaluate territories on customer relevance, competitor crowding, credibility, proof, economics.

title: Step 3: Positioning & Differentiation Strategy
content:
Step 3 Positioning & Differentiation:
Positioning is the clear, relevant, credible reason the target customer prefers this brand over alternatives.
Positioning is an internal strategic decision, NOT a public tagline.
Components: For whom, in what category, what need, what distinct value, compared with what, why believe it.
Quality tests: Relevant, Distinct, Credible, Defensible, Deliverable, Memorable, Focused.
Parity points (must be good enough) vs Difference points (meaningfully better). Table stakes must not be treated as differentiation.

title: Step 4: Value Proposition, Brand Promise & Proof Logic
content:
Step 4 Value Proposition & Brand Promise:
- Value Proposition layers: Functional (practical result), Emotional (how customer feels), Social (status/identity), Economic (ROI/savings).
- Brand Promise: The central commitment the brand consistently delivers. Promise is an operational obligation, not marketing fluff. Must pass delivery tests (product, ops, service). Reject overpromising.
- Reasons to Believe (Proof Hierarchy): Actual outcome > Independent validation > Measurement > Customer evidence > Process proof > Credential > Claim only.
Mark PROOF_GAP when promise lacks verifiable proof.

title: Step 5: Strategic Pillars, Boundaries & Choice Architecture
content:
Step 5 captures:
- Strategic Pillars: 3 to 5 operational principles the brand consistently delivers (e.g. 'Reliable quality without specialist complexity', NOT generic words like 'Quality').
- Brand Boundaries: What the brand deliberately will not become (protects coherence).
- Will Not Compete On (e.g. lowest price, maximum features, extreme customization).
- Must Be (core non-negotiable behaviors) vs Must Not Be (dangerous drift).
- Coherence tests across target, price, operations, product, and channel.

title: Step 6: Strategy Validation, Decision Lock & Risks
content:
Step 6 Strategy Validation:
Pass 10 tests: Customer relevance, Market fit, Competitive distinction, Business fit, Proofability, Economic fit, Deliverability, Coherence, Focus, Long-term usefulness.
Risks documented with severity and mitigation. Validation experiment cards for uncertain elements (concept test, message test, offer test).
Strategy Lock: Status LOCKED with versioning. Changes require documented reasons and evidence (no silent overwriting).

Q. بریف هویت برند برای فاز ۴ (Phase 4 Identity Brief)

title: Phase 4 Handoff: Identity Strategy Brief
content:
Handoff to Phase 4: Identity Strategy Brief (بریف استراتژی هویت برند).
Feeds directly into Phase 4 (Brand Identity & Character).
Contains: Business context, primary/secondary target, customer problem, category frame, competitive reference, strategic territory, positioning statement, core differentiation, parity/difference points, value proposition, brand promise, reasons to believe, strategic pillars, brand boundaries (must be, must not be, will not compete on), customer language, emotional direction, key risks, proof gaps, locked decisions.

title: Phase 3 Quality Gate & 20 Failure Modes
content:
Phase 3 Completion Gate: Target selected, Category frame selected, Competitive reference selected, Positioning selected, Differentiation defined, Value proposition defined, Brand promise defined, Proof logic defined, Pillars defined, Boundaries defined, Risks documented, Identity Strategy Brief ready.
Top Failure Modes:
1. Everyone is target. 2. Generic positioning. 3. Copying competitors. 4. Founder taste over evidence. 5. Too many benefits. 6. Strategy without trade-offs. 7. Promise without delivery. 8. Difference without value. 9. Words without proof. 10. Positioning contradicts price/operations.
Ultimate Rule: Phase 3 is where evidence becomes choice.

title: Phase 4 Mission, Scope & Core Principles
content:
Phase 4: Brand Identity Strategy & Brand Character (digital-market-brand-identity-character).
Primary Input: Brand Strategy Foundation and Identity Strategy Brief from Phase 3.
Primary Output: Brand Identity & Character Foundation (Persian) and Verbal Identity Brief handoff for Phase 5.
Mission: Translate strategic meaning into a human-like brand character, behavioral principles, emotional expression, relational role, communication posture, and creative guardrails.
Strict Boundary: Phase 4 does NOT finalize brand name, tagline, copywriting, logo, colors, typography, UI, packaging, or campaigns. Identity is not decoration or a mascot; it is how strategy behaves and communicates.

title: Step 0: Identity Readiness & Strategy Translation
content:
Step 0 Identity Readiness & Translation:
Requires Phase 3 locked strategy (Target, Positioning, Value Proposition, Promise, Pillars, Boundaries).
Strategy-to-identity mapping: What behavior makes positioning believable? What emotion supports value prop?
Category convention audit: Useful expectations, neutral conventions, crowded cliches, trust signals.
Identify identity opportunities (e.g. accessible expertise where competitors use formal jargon) and constraints.

title: Step 1: Brand Core Meaning & Identity Territory
content:
Step 1 Core Meaning & Territory:
Core Meaning layers: Functional, Emotional (how customer feels), Social, Symbolic.
Identity Territory: The emotional and expressive space within which the brand consistently lives (e.g. calm mastery, accessible expertise, thoughtful simplicity).
Anti-pattern: Random buzzwords (modern, premium, friendly, bold).
Desired customer emotional outcome: Specific state (e.g. 'I feel capable and informed, not overwhelmed').

title: Step 2: Brand Personality & Character System
content:
Step 2 Brand Personality System:
Trait Hierarchy:
- PRIMARY: 3 to 4 actionable traits driving decisions.
- SUPPORTING: Nuance providers.
- PROHIBITED: Explicitly forbidden traits (arrogant, elitist, childish, cold).
Trait Structure: Meaning, observable behavior, communication effect, experience effect, what it is not, risk of overuse.
Trait Tension: Prevents one-dimensional brand (e.g. Expert + Approachable, Warm + Precise).
Personality sliders: Formal/Informal, Reserved/Expressive, Calm/Energetic, etc.
Archetypes: Optional reference only, never replace custom character system. Define character under pressure (errors, complaints) and success.

title: Step 3: Brand Relationship, Role & Behavioral Principles
content:
Step 3 Brand Relationship & Behavior:
- Relationship Role: Guide, Partner, Coach, Enabler, Host, Ally, Curator, etc.
- Relationship Distance (Close, Warm-professional, Professional, Formal) & Authority Style (Leads, Guides, Advises, Collaborates, Serves).
- 4 to 7 Behavioral Principles: Actionable rules (e.g. 'Explain before persuading').
- Behavior in situations: Sales (advisory vs urgency), Support (empathy + resolution), Mistakes (Acknowledge -> Own -> Explain -> Fix -> Follow up -> Learn), Crisis posture.

title: Step 4: Communication Posture & Tone Boundaries
content:
Step 4 Communication Posture:
Voice is stable character; Tone is situational adjustment.
Posture dimensions: Formality, Warmth, Directness, Confidence (proof-backed, not hype), Energy, Expertise, Humor boundary, Emotionality, Simplicity.
Always / Sometimes / Never model for communication.
Persian language rules: Formality level, colloquial usage guidelines, English loanword policies, technical jargon handling.

title: Step 5: Identity Principles, Experience Signals & Guardrails
content:
Step 5 Identity Principles & Guardrails:
4 to 7 Identity Principles with implications across verbal, visual impression, and customer experience.
Experience Signals: Tangible moments at touchpoints (transparent pricing, fast clear onboarding, proactive updates).
Creative Guardrails:
- Must Feel Like (e.g. clear, assured, intelligent, warm).
- Must Not Feel Like (e.g. generic, flashy, cold, elitist, chaotic).
Elasticity: Stable elements (core meaning, primary traits, promise) vs Flexible elements (tone, energy, formality by channel).

title: Step 6: Identity Validation, Lock & Decision Rules
content:
Step 6 Validation & Lock:
Pass 11 tests: Strategy fit, Customer fit, Category fit, Distinctiveness, Credibility, Behavioral usability, Verbal usability, Visual usability, Experience usability, Flexibility, Coherence.
Identity Risk Map: Too generic, too formal, too casual, too technical, cultural mismatch.
Identity Lock: Status LOCKED with versioning. Changes require documented reasons and evidence.

title: Phase 5 Handoff: Verbal Identity Brief
content:
Handoff to Phase 5: Verbal Identity Brief (بریف هویت کلامی و پیام‌رسانی).
Feeds directly into Phase 5 (Verbal Identity & Messaging System).
Contains: Strategic context, positioning, core meaning, identity territory, primary/supporting/prohibited traits, relationship role, behavioral principles, communication posture, tone boundaries (always, sometimes, never), customer language, vocabulary constraints, technical language policy, must sound like vs must not sound like, identity principles, creative guardrails, proof requirements, messaging risks.

title: Phase 4 Quality Gate & Failure Modes
content:
Phase 4 Completion Gate: Core meaning defined, Identity territory selected, Personality defined, Relationship role defined, Behavioral principles defined, Communication posture defined, Tone boundaries defined, Identity principles defined, Creative guardrails defined, Risks documented, Verbal Identity Brief ready.
Top Failure Modes:
1. Generic personality. 2. Too many traits. 3. Personality conflicts with positioning. 4. Tone = personality. 5. Identity = visual style. 6. Founder mood dictates identity. 7. Category cliches. 8. Brand sounds different everywhere. 9. False humanization. 10. Archetype dogma.
Ultimate Rule: Phase 4 defines who the brand is before deciding exactly what the brand says or how the brand looks.

title: Phase 5 Mission, Scope & Core Concepts
content:
Phase 5: Verbal Identity & Messaging System (digital-market-verbal-identity-messaging).
Primary Input: Brand Identity & Character Foundation and Verbal Identity Brief from Phase 4.
Primary Output: Verbal Identity & Messaging System (Persian) and Creative & Naming Brief handoff for Phase 6.
Mission: Translate brand character into a complete verbal identity and messaging architecture (voice, situational tone, message hierarchy, core messages, value communication, proof language, brand story, pitch, vocabulary, and writing rules).
Strict Boundary: Phase 5 does NOT finalize brand name, logo, colors, typography, UI, packaging, or full campaign creative.

title: Voice vs Tone & Messaging vs Copy
content:
Voice vs Tone:
- VOICE: Stable verbal personality (always recognizable across touchpoints).
- TONE: Situational adjustment (calmer in support, higher energy in launch, measured in crisis).
Messaging vs Copy: Messaging is the strategic system of what the brand communicates; Copy is a specific execution.
Claims Rule: Separate Fact, Provable Claim, Strategic Message, Aspirational Language, and Hypothesis. Never write aspirational language as fact.

title: Step 0: Verbal Readiness & Identity Translation
content:
Step 0 Identity-to-Language Translation:
Maps personality traits and relationship role (e.g. Guide vs Expert) into verbal behaviors.
Establishes early guardrails: Must Sound Like vs Must Not Sound Like.
Customer language intake from Phase 2 (problem language, outcome language, objections).
Category language audit and cliché detection (banning empty words like 'best quality', 'innovative solutions' without proof).

title: Step 1: Brand Voice System & Principles
content:
Step 1 Brand Voice System:
3 to 5 core voice principles (e.g. 'Clear before clever').
Structure per principle: Meaning, why, how it sounds, how it does not sound, Do, Don't, and Before/After examples in Persian.
Traits: Primary, Supporting, Prohibited.
Verbal tensions prevent flat copy: Expert but Simple, Confident but Not Arrogant, Warm but Not Overfamiliar, Direct but Not Rude.

title: Step 2: Tone of Voice Matrix & Situational Adaptation
content:
Step 2 Situational Tone Matrix:
Default tone vs Contexts (Marketing, Sales, Education, Product/UI, Support, Complaint, Crisis, Celebration, B2B formal).
Tone dimensions: Formality, Warmth, Directness, Energy, Urgency, Emotionality, Humor, Technical depth.
Complaint tone: Reduce promotional energy, increase ownership and empathy, no defensive language.
Crisis tone: Accuracy before personality, clarity before cleverness, responsibility before promotion.

title: Step 3: Messaging Architecture & Message Hierarchy
content:
Step 3 Messaging Hierarchy:
Core Message (Why the primary target should care, connecting need + value + difference).
3 to 5 Message Pillars derived from value proposition and differentiation.
Feature to Benefit chain: Feature -> Functional Benefit -> Customer Outcome -> Emotional/Economic Value.
Journey-stage mapping: Awareness (problem/category), Consideration (differentiation/proof), Purchase (friction reduction/risk reversal), Retention (value realization).

title: Step 4: Core Messages, Proof Language & Objections
content:
Step 4 Core Messages & Proof Library:
Problem message, Desired outcome message, Value proposition message, Differentiation message, Brand promise message.
Proof & Claim System: Proof hierarchy (data, credentials, customer evidence, transparent process).
Unsupported Superlative Rule: Prohibit 'best', 'first', 'only', 'number one' unless verified by strong evidence.
Objection handling structure: Acknowledge -> Clarify -> Explain -> Prove -> Offer next step.

title: Step 5: Brand Story, One-Liner & Elevator Pitch
content:
Step 5 Core Narratives:
- One-Liner: Who we help + what we help them achieve + why we are different (concise, memorable).
- Short Brand Description: 2 to 4 sentences for directories and profiles.
- Elevator Pitch: 30-60 second spoken explanation (must sound natural and conversational).
- Brand Story: Customer as the hero, Brand as the guide/enabler. Factual origin (no fabricated history).
- About Narrative: Comprehensive story for website and corporate touchpoints.

title: Step 6: Vocabulary, Persian Rules, CTA & Channel Adaptation
content:
Step 6 Writing System & Execution:
- Vocabulary System: Preferred words, category terms, customer terms, words to avoid, prohibited claims.
- Persian Writing Rules: Formality level, pronoun choice (شما vs تو), English loanword policy, punctuation, emoji policy, digits, currency (تومان vs ریال).
- CTA System: Principles, types (learn, try, buy, etc.), low vs high commitment, no false urgency.
- Channel Adaptation: Guidelines for Website, Social, Sales, Support, Product/UI, Email, Advertising. Multilingual rules.

title: Step 7: Validation, QA Checklist & Governance
content:
Step 7 Governance & Lock:
Pass 12 validation tests: Strategy fit, Identity fit, Customer clarity, Distinctiveness, Proof integrity, Consistency, Writer usability, Scalability, etc.
Messaging QA Checklist: Key questions before publishing copy.
AI Copywriting Guardrails: Never invent customer numbers, awards, certifications, or guarantees.
Status LOCKED with versioning.

content:
Final Deliverable: Verbal Identity & Messaging System (سیستم هویت کلامی و معماری پیام‌رسانی).
Mandatory Persian (Farsi), beginner-friendly, fully downloadable.
28 Required Sections (A to AB):
A. خلاصه اجرایی (Executive Summary)

title: Phase 6 Handoff: Creative & Naming Brief
content:
Handoff to Phase 6: Creative & Naming Brief (بریف خلاقیت و نام‌گذاری برند).
Feeds directly into Phase 6 (Naming, Tagline & Creative Direction).
Contains: Strategic context, positioning, personality, voice, core message, one-liner, preferred/prohibited vocabulary, customer language, naming language constraints, what name must/must not signal, tagline territories, visual must-feel-like / must-not-feel-like, proof requirements, cultural & multilingual constraints, legal notes.

title: Phase 5 Quality Gate & 20 Failure Modes
content:
Phase 5 Completion Gate: Voice locked, Tone system locked, Hierarchy locked, Core messages locked, Proof language defined, One-liner defined, Elevator pitch defined, Brand story defined, Vocabulary defined, Writing rules defined, CTA defined, Channels adapted, Risks documented, Phase 6 Brief ready.
Top Failure Modes:
1. Voice is only adjectives. 2. Tone same everywhere. 3. Voice changes by channel. 4. Feature dump. 5. Generic core message. 6. Claims without proof. 7. Corporate jargon. 8. Excessive English. 9. Fiction brand story. 10. Fake urgency. 11. Boastful proof. 12. Competitor clone.
Ultimate Rule: Phase 5 defines exactly how the brand should sound and what it must communicate before creative naming and visual execution begin.

title: Phase 6 Mission, Scope & Critical Boundaries
content:
Phase 6: Naming, Tagline & Creative Direction (digital-market-naming-tagline-creative-direction).
Primary Input: Verbal Identity & Messaging System and Creative & Naming Brief from Phase 5.
Primary Output: Naming, Tagline & Creative Direction Foundation (Persian) and Visual Identity Design Brief handoff for Phase 7.
Mission: Translate verbal strategy into a strategically appropriate brand name, evaluated shortlist, clear tagline direction, and creative concept system.
Strict Boundary: Phase 6 does NOT finalize legal trademark registration, final domain purchase, logo design, color palette, typography, or UI design.

title: Step 0: Naming & Creative Readiness
content:
Step 0 Naming Readiness:
Imports what name must/must not signal, category, positioning, personality, language requirements (Persian & Latin script).
Naming jobs: Recognition, category signal, benefit, emotion, origin, distinctiveness, expansion.
Existing name equity evaluation for rebrands (Keep, Refine, Rename, Test).

title: Step 1: Naming Strategy & Criteria Framework
content:
Step 1 Naming Strategy & Criteria:
12 Naming types: Descriptive, Suggestive, Evocative, Abstract, Invented, Compound, Metaphorical, Founder-based, Geographic, Acronym, Foreign language, Hybrid.
Evaluation Matrix: Must-have, Should-have, Nice-to-have, and Knockout rules (offensive meaning, pronunciation failure, legal conflict).
Phonetic & Semantic criteria: Syllables, vowel flow, Persian vs Latin transliteration, homophones, typos, digital search collisions.

title: Step 2: Naming Territory Development
content:
Step 2 Naming Territories:
4 to 8 conceptual sources derived from positioning, value prop, and core meaning (Functional, Emotional, Metaphorical, Origin, Sound/Invented, Category, Benefit, Personality).
Prevents random dictionary hunting and ensures conceptual diversity.

title: Step 3: Name Generation, Screening & Shortlisting
content:
Step 3 Generation & 6-Stage Screening:
Generates 30-100+ raw candidates (Diverge -> Screen -> Converge).
Screening stages: 1. Strategic, 2. Linguistic, 3. Semantic, 4. Cultural, 5. Digital/Domain, 6. Preliminary Legal.
Shortlist of 3 to 7 serious names with scorecards, pronunciation, and spelling.
Domain strategy (exact match, modified, country TLD).
Preliminary legal screening (flagging potential conflicts, but explicitly stating it does NOT replace official legal clearance).

title: Step 4: Tagline Strategy & Tagline Development
content:
Step 4 Tagline Strategy:
Tagline need test: NO_TAGLINE is a valid strategic choice.
Tagline jobs: Category clarity, Positioning, Promise, Benefit, Emotional meaning, Memory, Campaign platform.
Criteria: Clarity, voice fit, distinctiveness, translatability, no clichés (e.g. 'quality you can trust').
Shortlist of 3 to 5 taglines and recommended tagline or no-tagline decision.

title: Step 5: Creative Territory Development & Direction
content:
Step 5 Creative Territories:
2 to 4 conceptual territories guiding visual, verbal, and experiential design (not a logo sketch).
Central Idea (one sentence), Symbolic World, Metaphors.
Visual Impression Brief: Level of restraint, density, energy, precision, human vs technical balance.
Cliché audit: Rejecting overused symbols (leaf for eco, shield for security, handshake for partnership).
Visual Literalism Rule: Logo does NOT need to literally depict the product or name.

title: Step 6: Validation, Decision Lock & Pairing Tests
content:
Step 6 Validation & Lock:
System coherence tests: Name <-> Tagline <-> Positioning <-> Creative Direction.
Name/Descriptor and Name/Tagline pairing tests.
Negative association test and Search collision checks.
Status: LOCKED with versioning. Changes require documented reasons and downstream review.

title: Step 7: Phase 7 Visual Identity Handoff
content:
Step 7 Phase 7 Handoff: Visual Identity Design Brief (بریف طراحی سیستم هویت بصری).
Translates creative direction into design guardrails for future visual designers (logo, color palette, typography, graphic system, motion, packaging, guidelines).
Phase 6 tells designers what the brand must mean and feel like; Phase 7 creates what it actually looks like.

title: Phase 6 Quality Gate & 25 Failure Modes
content:
Phase 6 Completion Gate: Naming strategy ready, Territories ready, Screening complete, Name decision ready, Tagline ready, Creative direction ready, Risks documented, Phase 7 Brief ready.
Top Failure Modes:
1. Brainstorming before criteria. 2. Cool sound with no meaning. 3. Overly descriptive name. 4. Unpronounceable invented name. 5. Bad Latin transliteration. 6. Exact .com controls everything. 7. Domain safety mistaken for trademark clearance. 8. Generic tagline. 9. Creative direction = logo sketch. 10. Cliché symbols (leaf, shield, handshake).
Ultimate Rule: Phase 6 turns the brand's strategy, identity, and language into a memorable name system, a purposeful tagline decision, and a coherent creative direction — without prematurely designing the visual identity.

title: Business Decision Chain & 5 Knowledge Layers (L1-L5)
content:
Causal Decision Chain: Society -> Macroeconomics -> Market -> Customer -> Brand -> Marketing -> Sales -> CRM -> Management -> Finance/Ops.
Knowledge Layers: L1 Theory & Laws, L2 Frameworks, L3 Playbooks/SOPs, L4 Real Data & Benchmarks, L5 Internal Enterprise Assets.
Veto Rules: Unit Economics Veto (LTV/CAC >= 3, Payback <= 12m), Macro-Inflation Veto (Shrinkflation / Down-trading adjustments), Operations Bottleneck Veto (TOC flow subordination).

title: The 30 Canonical Foundations for Business Decision-Making
content: Comprehensive reference covering 30 global authorities: Society (Bourdieu, Giddens, Rogers, Hofstede); Economics (Varian, Mankiw, Kahneman, Thaler); Market Strategy (Porter, Rumelt, Christensen); Customer (Christensen JTBD, Fitzpatrick Mom Test, Osterwalder); Brand (Keller CBBE, Aaker, Sharp, Kapferer); Marketing (Kotler, Barden, Cialdini, Godin); Sales (Rackham SPIN, Dixon Challenger, Voss); Retention (Reichheld NPS, Fader); Management (Drucker, Grove OKRs); Finance/Ops (Brealey & Myers DCF/NPV, Goldratt TOC, Skok Unit Economics).

title: GraphRAG Cross-Domain Ontology & Multi-Hop Traversal
content:
GraphRAG Ontology Entities: MacroCondition, CulturalContext, MarketStructure, CustomerJob, CognitiveBias, BrandAsset, MarketingTactic, SalesMotion, RetentionMechanism, OperationalConstraint, FinancialMetric.
Semantic Edges: CONSTRAINS, AMPLIFIES, VALIDATES, TRIGGERS, MITIGATES, BOTTLENECKS, DRIVES_PROFITABILITY.
Archetypal chains traverse from macro inflation to behavioral loss aversion down to unbundled pricing and working capital solvency.

title: Conflict Resolution, Evidence Ladder & Authority Scoring
content:
5-Tier Evidence Hierarchy: Tier 1 (0.95-1.00) Replicated empirical meta-analysis; Tier 2 (0.85-0.94) Systematic field studies; Tier 3 (0.70-0.84) Conceptual models; Tier 4 (0.55-0.69) Practitioner tech playbooks; Tier 5 (<0.40) Anecdotes/blog fads (Rejected).
Clash Resolution: FMCG/Mass uses Sharp (Distinctiveness/Penetration); B2B/Premium uses Kotler/Keller (Differentiation/STP). Day-1 to Scale uses Penetration (80%); Mature SaaS prioritizes Churn minimization (<5%).

title: Iran Indigenous Market & Macroeconomic Data Sources
content:
Official Iran Data Sources: Statistical Center of Iran (amar.org.ir: CPI, household budget surveys, demographics); Central Bank of Iran (cbi.ir: M2 money supply, Nima/free currency, PPI); Codal.ir (Audited industrial gross/net margins and cash cycles); E-commerce center (eNamad/Shaparak transaction volumes).
Platform Benchmarks: Digikala (FMCG growth, down-trading, basket size); Cafe Bazaar (Android OS distribution, in-app spending); Snapp (BNPL installment surge); Yektanet/Tapsell (CTR, CPC, 85%+ mobile share under connectivity shifts).
